props.gloss_en: whoever says the sons of Eli sinned is simply mistaken
as it is said: 'and there the two sons of Eli, Chofni and Pinchas, were priests to the Lord' (I Sam 1:3)
how then do I uphold 'how they lay with the women'? since they delayed their bird-offerings so that they did not go to their husbands, Scripture credits them as if they lay with them

as it is said: 'and Achiya son of Achituv, brother of Ichavod, son of Pinchas son of Eli, the Lord's priest' (I Sam 14:3) -- is it possible that sin came to his hand and Scripture traces lineage to him?

'the Lord will cut off from the man who does this him that is awake and him that answers... and him that presents an offering' (Mal 2:12): if an Israelite, he will have none awake among the Sages nor answering among the disciples; if a priest, he will have no son who presents an offering
whoever says the sons of Samuel sinned is simply mistaken
as it is said: 'and his sons did not walk in his ways' (I Sam 8) -- in his ways they did not walk, but sin they did not either

how then do I uphold 'and they turned aside after gain'? they did not act as their father, who went round all the places of Israel judging them in their towns ('and he went from year to year in circuit...', I Sam 7:16); they sat in their own towns to increase the fees of their attendants and scribes
[whether the sons of Samuel sinned] is [parallel to] a dispute of tannaim
R' Meir: they asked for their portion with their mouths
R' Yehuda: they imposed merchandise upon householders
R' Akiva: they took an extra basket of tithe by force
R' Yosei: they took the gifts by force
